name: ADXL343BCCZ-RL7
title: Three-axis digital MEMS accelerometer, ±2 g to ±16 g
summary: A three-axis MEMS accelerometer with digital output over SPI (3- or 4-wire) or I2C. Ranges of ±2 g to ±16 g are selectable, with up to 13-bit resolution at a fixed 3.9 mg/LSB, and output rates of 0.1 Hz to 3200 Hz. Built-in single and double tap, activity, inactivity and free-fall detection drive two mappable interrupt pins, and a 32-level FIFO buffers samples. It runs from 2.0 V to 3.6 V with a 1.7 V to VS interface supply, drawing 23 µA to 140 µA, in a 3 mm × 5 mm × 1 mm 14-terminal LGA.

circuits.title: Application diagram
circuits.description: The accelerometer with its two supplies decoupled at the pins: CS from VS to ground and CIO from VDD I/O to ground. The serial pins go to a 3- or 4-wire SPI or an I2C host, and INT1 and INT2 go to the host's interrupt inputs. A 1 µF tantalum on VS and a 0.1 µF ceramic on VDD I/O are the recommended values; separate VS and VDD I/O supplies keep digital noise off VS.

parts.note: tantalum, close to the VS pin; 10 µF tantalum with 0.1 µF ceramic in parallel can lower noise
ceramic, close to the VDD I/O pin

notes: A resistor or ferrite bead of at most 100 Ω in series with VS can add decoupling.
Pin 3 may instead go to VS and pin 11 to ground.

circuits.title: 3-wire SPI connection
circuits.description: Three-wire SPI: CS, SCLK and a single bidirectional data line SDIO to the host's MOSI. Set the SPI bit (D6 of DATA_FORMAT) for this mode. SDO is not used by the host; a 10 kΩ resistor to VDD I/O or to GND on SDO is recommended.

circuits.title: 4-wire SPI connection
circuits.description: Four-wire SPI: CS, SCLK, SDI from the host's MOSI and SDO to the host's MISO. Clear the SPI bit (D6 of DATA_FORMAT) for this mode. The clock idles high (CPOL = 1, CPHA = 1), up to 5 MHz with at most 100 pF load.

circuits.title: SPI connection on a bus shared with other devices
circuits.description: When other SPI devices share the bus, their traffic can look like an I2C start to the accelerometer while its CS is high. An OR gate between the host's MOSI and SDIO, with the accelerometer's CS as the other input, holds SDIO high whenever CS is high, so nothing reaches the part until it is selected.

circuits.title: I2C connection, address 0x53
circuits.description: I2C: CS tied to VDD I/O selects I2C, and ALT ADDRESS grounded sets the 7-bit address to 0x53 (0xA6 write, 0xA7 read). SDA and SCL each need an external pull-up RP to VDD I/O, sized per the I2C-bus specification. Other devices on the bus must not run more than 0.3 V above VDD I/O.

parts.note: pull-up, sized per the I2C-bus specification
pull-up, sized per the I2C-bus specification

notes: With ALT ADDRESS tied high instead, the address is 0x1D (0x3A write, 0x3B read).

operation.text: A polysilicon proof mass, held over the wafer by polysilicon springs, moves under acceleration and unbalances differential capacitors formed by fixed plates and plates on the mass. Phase-sensitive demodulation gives the magnitude and sign. Both static acceleration (gravity, for tilt) and dynamic acceleration are measured.

Ranges ±2 g, ±4 g, ±8 g and ±16 g. In 10-bit mode the scale factor doubles with each range step; in full-resolution mode the scale stays at about 4 mg/LSB (3.9 mg/LSB) and the word grows to 13 bits at ±16 g. Output is 16-bit twos complement. 3.9 mg/LSB resolves tilt changes under 1.0°.

VS and VDD I/O may come up in either order without damage. VS must be at least VDD I/O. VDD I/O must be present for the part to stay off the bus. After VS rises the part sits in standby until the measure bit (D3 of POWER_CTL, 0x2D) is set; registers can be read and written in standby, and configuring there before entering measurement is the recommended order. Clearing measure returns to standby.

Current follows the output data rate. Setting LOW_POWER (D4 of BW_RATE) lowers the internal sampling rate for less current at slightly more noise; it helps only at 12.5 Hz to 400 Hz. Standby draws 0.1 µA typ, takes no measurements and keeps the FIFO contents. Auto sleep (THRESH_INACT, TIME_INACT, then AUTO_SLEEP and link in POWER_CTL) drops to the sub-12.5 Hz rates, about 23 µA at VS = 2.5 V.

The part is always a slave. CS tied to VDD I/O gives I2C; CS driven by a master gives SPI. CS has no default if left floating, so it must be tied or driven. Data the part sends back during writes is to be ignored.

3-wire or 4-wire, chosen by the SPI bit (D6 of DATA_FORMAT): 0 is 4-wire. Clock up to 5 MHz at 100 pF, CPOL = 1, CPHA = 1; SCLK idles high, data changes on the falling edge and is sampled on the rising edge. CS falls to start and rises to end a transfer. The first byte holds R/W, then the multiple-byte bit MB, then the six address bits; with MB set the address advances every eight clocks until CS rises. Non-sequential registers need CS raised between them. If the host's clock polarity is set after the part is powered, raise CS before changing it.

Standard (100 kHz) and fast (400 kHz) modes, single- and multi-byte reads and writes, following the UM10204 I2C-bus specification Rev. 03. Address 0x1D with ALT ADDRESS high (0x3A/0x3B), 0x53 with it grounded (0xA6/0xA7). No pin has an internal pull-up or pull-down, so CS must go to VDD I/O and ALT ADDRESS to VDD I/O or GND. A read starts with a write of the register address, then a repeated start (or stop and start) and the read address; the master ends with NACK.

operation.topic: Output data rate and bus speed
operation.text: At 400 kHz I2C the highest usable ODR is 800 Hz, scaling linearly with clock (200 Hz at 100 kHz). On SPI, 3200 Hz and 1600 Hz call for a clock of 2 MHz or more and 800 Hz for 400 kHz or more, the other rates in proportion (100 kHz for 200 Hz). Running a faster ODR than the bus supports drops samples or adds noise.

INT1 and INT2 are push-pull outputs, active high unless INT_INVERT (DATA_FORMAT) is set. Each function is enabled in INT_ENABLE (0x2E) and sent to INT1 (bit 0) or INT2 (bit 1) by INT_MAP (0x2F); functions on one pin are ORed. Set up a function and its mapping before enabling it, and disable it before changing it. Interrupts latch: the data ones clear when the data registers 0x32 to 0x37 are read until the condition is gone, the rest when INT_SOURCE (0x30) is read. DATA_READY, watermark and overrun always set their INT_SOURCE bits whatever INT_ENABLE holds.

DATA_READY: new data present. SINGLE_TAP: one event above THRESH_TAP shorter than DUR. DOUBLE_TAP: two such events, the second starting after Latent and within Window. Activity: above THRESH_ACT on any enabled axis. Inactivity: below THRESH_INACT on all enabled axes for longer than TIME_INACT (up to 255 s). FREE_FALL: all axes below THRESH_FF for longer than TIME_FF (up to 1.28 s), always dc-coupled. Watermark: FIFO count reaches the samples value. Overrun: unread data overwritten (in bypass, the data registers; otherwise, a full FIFO).

A 32-level FIFO with bypass, FIFO, stream and trigger modes, set by FIFO_MODE (D7:D6 of FIFO_CTL). Data are read through the DATAX/Y/Z registers, oldest first. Read all axes of a sample in one burst: a single-byte read loses the rest of that sample. Allow at least 5 µs from the end of a data read (the step from register 0x37 to 0x38, or CS rising) to the next FIFO or FIFO_STATUS read; SPI at 1.6 MHz or less meets this through the address byte, faster SPI needs CS raised in between (at 5 MHz the total needed is at most 3.4 µs). In trigger mode wait 5 µs after the trigger before reading; re-arm by going to bypass and back, which clears the FIFO. Up to 33 entries can be available, the extra one in the output filter.

SELF_TEST applies an electrostatic force to the mass that adds to any real acceleration. The shift grows with VS²; the scale-factor table corrects the 2.5 V limits for other supplies. The response is bimodal; the limits cover both modes. Run it in normal power at 100 Hz to 800 Hz or 3200 Hz (rate 0x0A to 0x0D, or 0x0F); below 100 Hz or at 1600 Hz results may fall outside the limits. Full resolution at ±16 g gives enough range; below ±8 g the range may be too small. Average about 0.1 s of data (at least 10 samples) with self-test off, then on after about four samples of settling. Reaching the minimum magnitude is a pass; exceeding the maximum is not necessarily a fail. Toggling self-test at a set rate and looking for that tone in an FFT removes the dependence on supply and magnitude.

A tap is above THRESH_TAP for no longer than DUR. A second tap must start after the Latent time and within Window, but need not end within it. The double tap is rejected if, with Suppress set, the signal crosses the threshold during Latent; if it is above threshold when Window opens; or if the second event outlasts DUR. With single tap alone, the interrupt fires when the signal drops below threshold within DUR; with both enabled, it fires once the double tap is accepted or rejected. Latent and Window must both be nonzero for double tap. Starting values: DUR above 0x10 (10 ms), Latent above 0x10 (20 ms), Window above 0x40 (80 ms), THRESH_TAP above 0x30 (3 g); very low values can pick up echoes. ACT_TAP_STATUS (0x2B) records the first axis over threshold and is overwritten, never cleared; read it before clearing the interrupt.

Low output rates come from decimating one internal sampling rate. Activity, free-fall and tap work on the undecimated data, so they can trigger on fast, high-g content that does not show in the output data. Inactivity works on the filtered output, needs at least one output sample, and looks slow if TIME_INACT is below the output period.

ACT ac/dc and INACT ac/dc: 0 compares the acceleration directly with the threshold; 1 compares the change from a reference. For activity the reference is taken when detection starts; for inactivity it is refreshed whenever the threshold is exceeded. Enabled axes are ORed for activity and ANDed for inactivity; with no axis enabled the function is off.

Link (D5 of POWER_CTL) makes activity wait for inactivity and inactivity wait for activity, cutting interrupts the host must handle; the host must still clear each by reading INT_SOURCE, and an uncleared activity interrupt blocks auto sleep. AUTO_SLEEP, with link set, enters sleep on inactivity and wakes on activity at the BW_RATE rate. Sleep suppresses DATA_READY, stops FIFO filling and samples at the wakeup rate (8, 4, 2 or 1 Hz); only activity works. After clearing link, AUTO_SLEEP or sleep, go to standby and back to measurement in a later write, or the first samples may be noisy. For data collection at low rate and low power, low power mode keeps DATA_READY and the FIFO; sleep mode is not meant for data acquisition.

DATAx0 is the low byte and DATAx1 the high byte of each axis, twos complement. Read all six in one multi-byte access so they come from the same sample. Justify 1 gives left-justified (MSB) data, 0 right-justified with sign extension. Data in every range but ±16 g need clipping so they do not wrap around. At 3200 Hz and 1600 Hz in full resolution or ±2 g 10-bit mode the lowest bit is always 0 (D0 of DATAx0 right-justified; left-justified it moves to D6, D5, D4 or D3 of DATAx0 for ±2, ±4, ±8 and ±16 g). In 10-bit ±4, ±8 and ±16 g, and at 800 Hz or below in any mode, every bit is valid. Right-justified, the ±4 g and ±8 g full-resolution words have their MSB at D2 and D3 of DATAx1.

Assembly stress (soldering, board mounting, coatings) shifts the 0 g offset, so calibrate after assembly. One-point method: z axis in +1 g, x and y in 0 g, average about 0.1 s (10 samples at 100 Hz, at least 10 below 100 Hz), and write the negated, rounded result to OFSX/OFSY/OFSZ at 15.6 mg/LSB, independent of range. The offset registers are added to the data and lose their value at power-off (reset 0x00). A sensitivity error turns into a z offset error (250 LSB/g instead of 256 would give 15 LSB, not 9); a second point with z in 0 g removes it.

1.1 LSB rms typ at 100 Hz, normal power. At 400 Hz, under 1.5 LSB rms on x and y and under 2.2 on z. In low power mode the noise is the same at every listed rate: under 1.8 LSB rms on x and y and under 2.6 on z. Noise density is 290 µg/√Hz on x and y and 430 µg/√Hz on z; the 1/f corner is low enough for about 100 µg absolute resolution with long averaging. Noise falls as VS rises, by about the same percentage on all axes.

Specified at VS = 2.5 V, usable from 2.0 V to 3.6 V. At 3.3 V the x and y offset is typically 25 mg higher and z 20 mg lower than at 2.5 V; x and y sensitivity rises from 256 to 265 LSB/g while z is unchanged. Interpolate linearly for other supplies. Current follows the trend of the supply current curve at all rates.
Below 6.25 Hz ODR the offset drifts much more with temperature than at higher rates. Limit the temperature range and calibrate over temperature when using these rates.
Keep the ground return to the supply low impedance, since ground noise acts like supply noise. Separate VS and VDD I/O supplies avoid digital clock noise on VS; otherwise filter the supplies.

Place the part near a hard mounting point of the board to its case. On an unsupported part of the board, board vibration shows as large errors; near a mounting point the board resonance stays above the sensor's mechanical resonance. More mounting points near the sensor or a thicker board also help.
The output rises when the part is accelerated along a sensitive axis. At rest with one axis vertical, that axis reads +1 g or −1 g depending on which way it points and the other two read 0 g.
